course_name_original: Dirección y Gestión de Empresas de Base Tecnológica
course_name_en: Management and Administration of Technology-Based Companies
prerequisites: Ability to read and comprehend documentation written in English.

learning_outcomes.text: Capacity for strategic planning, elaboration, direction, coordination, and technical and economic management in the fields of computer engineering related to systems, applications, services, networks, IT infrastructures or facilities, and software development centers or factories, ensuring proper compliance with quality and environmental criteria in multidisciplinary work environments.
Know the structure and functioning of a technology-based company.
Know the techniques of direction, coordination, and technical-economic management of companies.
Plan the development and commercialization strategy for ICT products and services.

syllabus_topics: Concept and characteristics of technology-based companies
Differences between TBC and traditional companies
Innovation ecosystems and the role of TBCs in the economy
Entrepreneurship and creation of a Technology-Based Company
Technological entrepreneurship and generation of business opportunities
Innovation and development of technology-based business models in the context of responsible innovation in the EU
Evaluation of the viability of a technological business model
Strategic management, decision making, and technological transformation
Strategic management and decision making in technology-based companies
Technological transformation and advanced analytics for business management
Responsible digital transformation, governance, and responsible use of data in the company within the framework of the European Union
The financial subsystem in technology-based companies
Financing and investment decisions in TBCs
Sources of financing and access to capital for technology companies

assessment_methods.method: Group work (P3) (business idea development and business plan presentation)

assessment_rules: For ordinary examination, a minimum grade of 4 out of 10 is required for both the theoretical and practical blocks. The theoretical block contributes 40% of the final grade (0.4 x T1), and the practical block contributes 60% (0.2 x P1 + 0.2 x P2 + 0.2 x P3). The final grade is the sum of the theoretical and practical block grades, provided the minimums are met; otherwise, the final grade will be the minimum between the calculated grade and 4.0. For extraordinary examination or differentiated evaluation, the assessment consists of a final exam and a practical assignment. A minimum of 4 out of 10 points is required for each part. If these minimums are met, the final grade is calculated as (0.4 x Exam) + (0.6 x Practical Assignment); otherwise, the final grade will be the minimum between the calculated grade and 4.0. Students who met the minimums in the practical block during ordinary examination may choose to retain those grades and only take the theoretical exam, which will then have a weight of 4 points, with the same minimum criteria applied.
